sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever felt like `if-else` chains are getting too messy? Let’s learn a cleaner way to handle multiple choices!

• How `switch` statements simplify multi-way branching
• When to use `switch` vs `if-else`
• The magic of `break` and `default` cases

sections.title: Core Concepts
Code Examples
Key Points
points: switch evaluates an expression and jumps to the matching case label
Each case should end with break to prevent fall-through to the next case
The default case executes when no other case matches
switch works with int, char, String, and enum types (not double or boolean)
switch is cleaner than multi-way if-else when comparing one variable to many constants

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: `switch` simplifies multi-way branching with clean syntax. `break` stops fall-through; `default` handles edge cases. Practice with real-world menus or game controls. Ready to combine with loops next.

questions.question: What keyword is used to exit a case block in a switch statement?
questions.explanation: The 'break' keyword exits a case block in a switch statement. Without break, execution 'falls through' into the next case block.

questions.question: What happens if you omit the break statement in a switch case?
options: Execution falls through to subsequent cases
questions.explanation: Without a break statement, execution falls through from the matched case into the subsequent cases until a break is encountered or the switch block ends.
